title: Follow-up results (exploratory): Enforcing Document Permissions in Vector Search, an Experimental Comparison
description: The exploratory follow-up runs registered, before any of them ran, in addendum 1 to the pre-registration (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24406063; the pre-registration itself is https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24026269). They measure each store's filter and the post-filters at three settings of search breadth (ef 40, 100 and 400) and pgvector with raised iterative-scan limits; the cost of looking up a user's principals in SpiceDB or OpenFGA for the arms that filter in the store; p50 and p99 latency per job; and a diagnostic of the permission-change protocol with SpiceDB's at_least_as_fresh and fully_consistent reads. They extend the measured results of release results-v1 (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24055691), whose cells at ef 100 they also re-measure. This version archives the repository (the harness and bench.followup, which made the report) at the GitHub release it was made from. The raw outputs of every follow-up job and the report are assets of that GitHub release (results-raw.tar.gz and report.tar.gz, with SHA256SUMS covering both), not files of this record; report/collected.tsv lists every job with its workflow run, and report/followup.md presents the report. The raw outputs hold identifiers, scores, timings and plan shapes, not passage or message text; the workloads they refer to are the releases data-msmarco-v1 (derived from MS MARCO, non-commercial research only under its terms) and data-enron-v2 (derived from the CMU Enron corpus) of the repository. Code and history: https://github.com/muzakkirhussain011/rag-permission-bench. The study includes wardowl, the author's own library, as one arm; this is a declared conflict of interest.
